mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.3 percentage points within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent month-over-month increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) for three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS increased for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month indicates a contraction in supply, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic output slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO declined by more than 1% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a low federal funds rate (below 2%) signals accommodative monetary policy, which typically supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as cheap borrowing costs fuel investment.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the periods where FEDFUNDS was below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and a decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) within a month signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases and UNRATE decreases in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where HOUST increased and UNRATE decreased within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional mechanism where a decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, but only during an economic expansion.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS decreased by more than 100,000 during an economic expansion.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) and a decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) within a month signals a potential inflationary environment with accommodative monetary policy, which historically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases and FEDFUNDS decreases in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where CPIAUCSL increased and FEDFUNDS decreased within a month.
